methodological_rigor.justification: International randomized phase III noninferiority trial (N=6,088) comparing 3 vs 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy for CRC. Randomization 1:1, stratification by treatment regimen (CAPOX vs FOLFOX), sex, disease site, T/N stage. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models with prespecified minimization factors. Proper noninferiority design with prespecified HR margin (1.13). Proportionality of hazards verified; restricted mean survival time models used when violated. Long follow-up (median 113 months) with mature OS data (1,255 events). Limitations: open-label design, secondary analyses by regimen increase type I error risk.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: International randomized controlled trial demonstrating noninferiority of 3 months versus 6 months of adjuvant oxaliplatin-fluoropyrimidine chemotherapy for CRC with long-term follow-up (15-year OS 82.4% both arms). Directly addresses clinically important question: Can treatment duration be reduced to mitigate cumulative peripheral neuropathy without compromising efficacy? Findings support practice change with major implications for patient quality of life. High-risk stage III disease showed small absolute OS difference (2.2%) favoring 6 months but insufficient to override toxicity concerns.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive CONSORT-compliant reporting with clear description of randomization (1:1), stratification factors, endpoints (DFS, OS), statistical approach (Cox models, noninferiority testing), and subgroup analyses. CONSORT diagram provided. Long-term follow-up methodology clearly described. Kaplan-Meier curves and forest plots effectively communicate results. Trial registered (ISRCTN59757862). Data availability through international trial collaboration; individual-level data sharing mechanisms not explicitly stated.

novelty_literature.justification: Largest of IDEA collaboration trials (six pooled studies) and only individual trial confirming noninferiority of 3 months of adjuvant chemotherapy. Extends prior pooled analysis with largest CAPOX proportion (67.5%) and only study including rectal cancer. Long-term follow-up (15 years) provides durability evidence. Regimen-dependent effect (noninferiority for CAPOX but not FOLFOX) novel finding refining treatment recommendations, though somewhat incremental given prior IDEA pooling publication.

writing_presentation.justification: Clear manuscript structure with well-motivated introduction contextualizing need for treatment de-escalation, comprehensive Methods section detailing randomization and statistical approach, Results systematically presenting DFS, OS by duration and subgroup (regimen, risk, disease site), and Discussion appropriately contextualizing findings. Forest plot effectively displays subgroup results. Limitations appropriately acknowledged (open-label, secondary analyses). Writing accessible to clinical audience.

key_strengths: Large international RCT (N=6,088) with 15-year median follow-up and mature OS data (1,255 events) demonstrating noninferiority of 3 months vs 6 months adjuvant chemotherapy
Demonstrates 5-year OS 82.4% both arms; noninferiority formally confirmed (p=0.0033); 2.4% absolute OS difference for high-risk disease insufficient to warrant additional toxicity burden
Regimen-dependent effect identified: noninferiority shown for CAPOX (most common, 67.5%) but not FOLFOX, enabling treatment refinement

Direct clinical relevance: reduces cumulative peripheral neuropathy (25% to 58% grade ≥2) with improved quality of life while maintaining OS benefit; 50 needed to treat to prevent one death vs 15 needed to prevent one case of neuropathy
Rigorous methodology: multivariable Cox models with prespecified stratification factors, verification of proportional hazards, sensitivity analyses with restricted mean survival time
key_concerns: Open-label design creates potential for investigator bias in secondary assessments, though OS objective endpoint minimizes concern
Secondary analyses by regimen increase type I error risk; FOLFOX-treated patients may warrant different considerations but analyzed as secondary endpoint
Rectal cancer subgroup (n=1,087) showed noninferiority for CAPOX but limited FOLFOX data (small subgroup); generalizability to all rectal cancers unclear
Absolute OS differences modest (1.4-2.4%) across most subgroups; clinical significance of observed differences beyond noninferiority margin debatable
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 1 appropriate for large, rigorous international RCT with mature long-term outcomes establishing noninferiority and demonstrating practice-changing benefit (reduced toxicity without OS compromise). High-quality methodology, large sample, extended follow-up, and direct clinical relevance support Tier 1 publication in top venue (JAMA, Lancet, JCO).
